followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability:** Petrel is the stronger model across essentially every relevant metric — Creative Generation (85.9 vs 78.8), Summarization, Support Dialogue, and all public benchmarks. Since this query involves composing a persuasive, well-structured personal pitch (a generative/creative writing task), Petrel's edge there directly serves the task.

**Preference:** The request is friendly and warm in tone ("I'd really appreciate," "Thanks so much"), and it's an open-ended composition task — exactly the kind of generative work Petrel self-reports preferring. Petrel's preference also declines on hostile-tone requests, but this query is the opposite of hostile, so there's no friction.

There was also no reason *not* to send it to Petrel: the content is completely benign, so Petrel's strong aversion to harm-adjacent material (the one area where it might balk and Curlew would be neutral) is irrelevant here.

So Petrel wins on both axes — better capability for the task and well-aligned preferences — with no countervailing concerns. Curlew's main distinguishing feature is its flat response to harm-adjacent content, which simply doesn't apply to a job-application writing request.
